problem:
Which of the following systems are homogeneous?

- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t)+1\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=5{x}_{1}(t)+6{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t)+{e}^{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t)+3t\end{aligned}$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following systems are homogeneous?

- ${x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)$
- ${x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
- ${x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}]$
feedback.worked_solution:
In matrix form, the system

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=A(t)x(t)+f(t)
$$

is *homogeneous* when $f≡0,$ and *inhomogeneous* when $f≢0.$

With this in mind, let's inspect each system:

- System I is homogeneous since $f≡0.$

- System II is inhomogeneous since $f=[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}]≢0.$

- System III is inhomogeneous since $f=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}]≢0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
